applicability.scope: Engines with multi-token speculative decoding whose verification forward cost grows with query rows
applicability.prerequisites: A calibrated per-position acceptance signal; a measured (rows, step_time) curve; a handle on metadata construction
applicability.hardware: Backend-independent procedure; the reference implementation targets NVIDIA SM100 and Ascend 950 only

limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation and no reproduced gain.
The reference budgets verification rows only; draft compute is unchanged.
The budgeted path is off by default in the reference source.
Budgeting can lower accepted length; equal accepted length is not an acceptance criterion.
Per-position independence of the confidence used for verification is a correctness requirement, not only a scheduling convenience.
Cross-backend rejection-comparison parity is unproven; the reference has no equality assertion.
Numeric acceptance rates and warmup curves are deployment-specific and are not carried here.
